source: hand-authored fixture for issue #310 — not shipped data
description: The arrangement in which de-duplicating the rendered clause LIST would, on its own, put a reading SECTION out of the list's order. Pethidine files three rules on three collapsed keys: a condition rule on 'hepatic impairment' carrying the note 'avoid in opioid-sensitive states', which this patient does not record; a condition rule on 'respiratory depression' carrying 'documented respiratory risk', which she does; and a SELF-NAMED allergy rule on 'pethidine' carrying that FIRST note again, which her recorded 'Pethidine' allergy both matches and names. So one clause string is rendered by two keys whose sections differ — the first key wants the denial and the third the assertion, and the cross-key precedence gives it to the assertion — with a SECOND string rendered between them by a key that also lands in the assertion. The list's own order is therefore first-occurrence order ('avoid …' then 'documented …') while the recorded section, walked per key, reaches 'documented …' first; contraindicationSections' own comment carries why that matters. (2) Tapentadol is the same anomaly in the OTHER two sections, which the recorded one cannot reach: a string can enter the DENIAL late because an earlier key rendering it was UNEVALUABLE (a rule of an unrecognised type renders a clause but claims no section of its own; where an evaluable rule renders the same string, that string is still claimed), and it can enter the HEDGE late because an earlier key rendering it was a denial (the hedge outranks the denial). Its first and third rules carry 'monitor for respiratory depression' with 'avoid in hepatic impairment' between them; its fourth and sixth carry 'dose reduction required' with 'documented tapentadol reaction' between them. The allergen 'Tapentazoline' reaches the self-named 'tapent' rule mid-word and names no entry, and the recorded condition 'Malignant tumor of adrenal gland' reaches the 'renal' rule inside 'adrenal' rather than at a word boundary, so both of those match without corroborating (issue #309's shape). No entry carries ATC codes or interactions, so nothing but the allergy and condition arms can speak.
